item.title: Remembering Joanne Wile, social worker, activist, mayor of Albany
item.description: As mayor and councilmember, she led on Albany-Berkeley waterfront issues. She worked for 27 years in UCSF and San Francisco General's psychiatry department.

item.title: How an Ohlone nonprofit quickly became one of the wealthiest Indigenous land trusts in the nation
item.description: With $54 million in assets, Sogorea Te' has big dreams for its reclaimed West Berkeley shellmound site. Its voluntary shuumi land tax has become wildly popular in the East Bay even as it's drawn criticism from other Ohlone groups that say the money doesn't reach the broader community.

item.title: The East Bay’s tastiest, most tantalizing SF Beer Week events
item.description: From multiple beer and cheese pairings, to speed dating, taste offs and wrestling, the 2026 Beer Week lineup has something for everyone.

item.title: Around Berkeley: Lunar New Year, youth orchestra concert, free wood chips
item.description: Other events include an author talk by antifascist and sex activist Kitty Stryker and a musical featuring two lovers bonding through music.

item.title: No-bid city contracts could be giving Berkeley a bad deal, audit finds
item.description: Berkeley spent tens of millions of dollars on non-competitive contracts for deals that should have gone out to bid, the city’s auditor found, though there was no evidence of corruption or favoritism.

item.title: Mt. Agni goes dark, plus the last East Bay outpost of a classic Italian deli has closed
item.description: A running list of restaurants that have recently closed in Berkeley, Oakland, Richmond, and beyond.

item.title: Update: Possible mumps exposure at 2 Berkeley schools, but city says risk of community transmission is ‘very low’
item.description: There were under 350 reported mumps cases in the U.S. last year, the CDC says. The alert comes amid rising misinformation about the vaccine against the contagious disease.

item.title: The Wire: Tabby cat adopted from Berkeley Humane is a top animal actor of the year
item.description: Also: A missing UC Berkeley student was found in Lake Anza and where the Amoeba Music apartment project stands.

item.title: Caught curling fever from the Olympics? Here’s where you can try it in the East Bay
item.description: Berkeleyside news editor Nico Savidge, who once joined a curling club while working at a Wisconsin newspaper, again ventured onto the ice at California's only dedicated curling facility, located in Oakland.

item.title: UC Berkeley cuts ties with nonprofit focused on diversity amid Trump administration pressure
item.description: It is one of 31 colleges that the Education Department says have ended relationships with The PhD Project, a nonprofit that for decades has helped Black, Latino and Native American students get business doctorates.
